cost.a: glot is MIT and free. You pay your LLM provider with your own key: 850 strings cost $0.035 with the default model in our run. glot translate --dry-run estimates first, and a budget caps it.

runtime.q: Does it add a runtime dependency?
runtime.a: No. Your app keeps next-intl, i18next or FormatJS with plain JSON catalogs. glot works on the files, in your repo and in CI.

fails.q: What if the model keeps getting a string wrong?
fails.a: glot sends the exact reason back and retries twice, then tries the fallback model. If it still fails, nothing is written: the key is reported as rejected and stays untranslated.

code.q: Does my code leave my machine?
code.a: The strings to translate and their context go to your LLM provider. Not your source files. Nothing goes to glot's authors; there is no telemetry.

app.q: Do I need the web app?
app.a: No. The CLI and the MCP server do the whole job locally. The app adds a shared dashboard, review and GitHub sync for teams.

foundation.cost: 850 strings cost $0.035 with the default model in our run. You pay your LLM provider directly.

what.a: glot is an open-source (MIT) CLI and MCP server that localizes your app with your own LLM key, plus copy experiments: AI-written versions of your headlines, checked in every locale and served to each audience. Code refuses any text that breaks a placeholder, a plural, your glossary or its UI box.

audiences.q: Can I show different copy to different countries?
audiences.a: Yes. glot serves several versions of a headline or button to the audiences you choose (country, device, traffic source), in every language at once, and keeps the one that converts. Up to 4 audiences per experiment, plus everyone else.

ai.a: Every variant goes through the same checks as your translations, in every locale, plus rules against fake urgency, invented numbers and unprovable claims. You can require a human approval before any variant goes live.

facts.q: Can a variant invent a stat or a discount?
facts.a: No. A variant may only cite the facts you declare. Any number not in your text or your facts is refused. Keys tagged as pricing or legal can't be tested at all.

speed.q: Does it slow my site down or flicker?
speed.a: No blocking call. The edge picks the version from a cached file and your server renders it, so there is no flicker with server rendering. Client-only single-page apps may flicker on first paint. If glot is down, visitors get your official text.

cookies.q: Do I need a cookie banner for this?
cookies.a: glot sets no cookie by default and stores no IP, user agent or visitor ID, only daily counts. An optional session cookie holds the version, nothing else. Whether you need consent is your DPO's call; our privacy notes help.

seo.q: Does showing different copy hurt SEO?
seo.a: glot never picks a version based on the user agent. Crawlers get a version like any visitor, on the same URL with the same canonical, and bot visits are not counted. Versions keep the same meaning.

traffic.q: How much traffic do I need?
traffic.a: It depends on your traffic and conversion rate. When you create an experiment, glot estimates how long it will take and suggests merging an audience that would need more than 90 days. Start with one global experiment.

winner.q: How do I know a winner is real?
winner.a: glot waits at least 7 days and 500 visitors per version, raises the bar each time it looks, and can keep a small holdout to measure everything you promoted.

cost.a: The CLI, the validator and the local MCP server are MIT and free; you pay your LLM provider directly. glot cloud has a free plan for one project, Pro for reliable localization in a team, and Growth for experiments and language launches measured on revenue. Self-host the server and nothing is limited.

formats.q: Which frameworks and file formats does glot support?
formats.a: Automatic string extraction: Next.js (App and Pages Router), React Router, Astro and Vite + React. Catalogs: JSON with ICU, i18next or MessageFormat 2 syntax, JS dictionaries, Apple .xcstrings and .strings, Android strings.xml, Flutter ARB, gettext PO and YAML.

agents.q: Which coding agents work with glot?
agents.a: Any agent that speaks MCP, such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or Windsurf, through npx -y glot-i18n mcp. Claude Code also has a glot plugin and skill, and AGENTS.md rules are provided for other agents.

oss.q: Is anything in the open-source tool limited?
oss.a: No. Quotas only apply to requests served by glot cloud. The CLI, the local MCP server and the GitHub Action never call the billing system.

byok.q: Do you mark up LLM costs?
byok.a: No. With your own key, you pay your LLM provider directly and glot neither counts nor marks up those translations. Without a key, the cloud can use glot's key: each plan includes a monthly amount, and monthly plans can continue beyond it with usage-based billing.

selfHost.a: Yes. The server is in the same MIT repository. Without Stripe keys, billing is off and every limit is lifted; you run and update it yourself.

limits.q: What happens when I reach a quota?
limits.a: The cloud endpoint answers 402 with a message and an upgrade link; your shipped catalogs keep working from your repository. Quotas reset on the 1st of each month (UTC).

tax.q: Are prices with or without VAT?
tax.a: Prices are shown without VAT. Stripe handles payments, invoices and VAT: VAT is added at checkout where it applies, and business customers can enter a VAT number. Invoices are in your billing settings.

quotas.a: Only what glot cloud serves: CDN/OTA requests, insights and experiment events, remote MCP calls, on-demand locale jobs, live review annotations and strings translated with glot's key. Live experiments and cloud projects count while they exist. Nothing you run locally, and nothing translated with your own key, is counted. Monthly counters reset on the 1st (UTC).

cancel.a: Yes, from the billing portal. Your plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for, then the account moves to Free. Projects and data are kept.
